name: Cryogenic silicon optical-resonator frequency interrogation across1.5–3.6 K (Wiens et al.2020)
plain_name: Measure frequency drift of a cryogenic silicon optical reference
description: Measure frequency drift of a cryogenic silicon optical reference. A bounded, source-grounded procedure profile; compatibility covers the listed checks and does not guarantee measured scientific performance.

sources.citation: Wiens et al. (2020), A simplified cryogenic optical resonator apparatus providing ultra-low frequency drift, Review of Scientific Instruments 91, 045112

requirements.rationale: Replicate the paper's temperature interval. These are this profile's reviewed procedure conditions, not a universal requirement for the scientific field.
Laser injection and transmitted-light detection need real optical paths. These are this profile's reviewed procedure conditions, not a universal requirement for the scientific field.

Frequency scans, transmission detection and a frequency reference are essential; a bare optical cryostat is insufficient. These are this profile's reviewed procedure conditions, not a universal requirement for the scientific field.

missing_information: Frequency-comb/maser reference, vibration transfer, optical heating and resonator mounting require separate review. No frequency-stability result is encoded as a compatibility guarantee.
The paper explicitly says the cryogenic PDH lock was not implemented; the scene uses repeated line scans or detuning interrogation.
confirmation_note: Profile author reviewed these exact sourced conditions on 2026-10-31. The application must still require the user's review/confirmation; all edits invalidate confirmation.
